newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE SICK AND TIRED AFTER 76 IN U.S. OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE SICK AND TIRED AFTER 76 IN U.S. OPEN.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie, who let the U.S. Open lead slip from his grasp on Friday, said he had no excuses for his bad play -- and then offered several.

The burly Briton, who scorched the treacherous Congressional Country Club course with a first-round 65, stumbled to a six-over-par 76 in the weather-interrupted second round, falling four shots behind British Open champion Tom Lehman.

Montgomerie, who had to wait for more than two hours to tee off when the threat of lightning suspended play, said the delay, some unruly spectators and the steamy weather all conspired the throw him off his game.

"The crowd was quite boisterous after the rain delay -- obviously they had been in certain (hospitality) tents -- and that didn't help matters, really," Montgomerie said after his round, which included six bogeys and no birdies.
Montgomerie, who flew here from England Monday after winning a European tour event Sunday, also said he had not felt up to par all week -- despite his par-busting performance on Thursday.
"I haven't felt well since I've been here, actually, and I don't feel well right now," he told reporters near the 18th green after closing with bogeys on the 16th and 17th holes.
Montgomerie, a veteran of three Ryder Cup campaigns, also said he was disturbed by some unruly spectators who cheered when he missed a birdie putt on the ninth hole.
"We expect that this game of golf is not that type of game," the 33-year-old Scot said. "That's usually saved for the Ryder Cup and not the U.S. Open.
"It was disappointing and it put me in the wrong frame of mind."
Montgomerie, who survived even hotter weather conditions when he played his way into the three-man playoff in the 1994 Open at Oakmont, said he developed a headache during his round due to the heat.
He said he tried to get some headache medication at one point but the staff in the medical tent on the course did not have any, he said.
"I tend to suffer more than most with the heat and humidity and stuff," he added.
Then he summed up his disappointing day.
"It's difficult to wait two and a half hours when you are leading the U.S. Open," he said. "It is very difficult."
